groups.title: Tablet (A18800ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for urticaria, eczema, itching and lacquer poisoning (rash from lacquer).
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 tablet per dose, 3 times in 1 day, after meals.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if the user is a child under 15 years of age, or if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have had hypersensitivity to an anti-allergy medicine, a cold medicine, an antitussive-expectorant or a motion-sickness medicine; if you have glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like) or difficulty passing urine; if you have a weak constitution, diarrhoea, loose stools or a markedly weak stomach; if you have loss of appetite, nausea or vomiting, or are markedly weakened; or if you have had hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to Yellow No. 5 or Sunset Yellow FCF.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery. Do not take it continuously for a long period.

Do not take it together with another laxative, an anti-allergy medicine or a medicine containing an antihistamine (motion-sickness medicine, cold medicine, antitussive-expectorant). Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with another herbal preparation (especially a preparation containing rhubarb).

If rash, reddening of the skin, thirst, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, stomach discomfort, abdominal pain or diarrhoea with severe abdominal pain occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist. Loose stools and the like may occur.

groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 2 capsules per dose, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby (newborn) under 3 months of age; or if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks.

Consult a pharmacist if the user is a child aged 3 months or older and under 2 years of age; if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution or have had an allergy caused by a medicine; if you have liver, kidney, heart or thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure or gastric or duodenal ulcer; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Do not take it continuously for a long period. If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like), an antitussive-expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative, or an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (oral medicine for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine). groups.title: Soft Capsule (142301ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for chronic polyarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, arthrosis, ankylosing spondylitis, painful swelling or inflammation after injury and surgery, and as an aid in the treatment of infections accompanied by inflammation, pain and fever.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 capsule (300 mg) per dose, 2 to 4 times in 1 day. Do not exceed 4 capsules (1200 mg) in 1 day.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and possibly fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration and perforation may occur.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have or have had gastrointestinal ulcer; if you have bleeding in the gastrointestinal tract, the cerebral blood vessels or elsewhere; if you have a severe blood disorder, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, severe cardiac insufficiency or severe high blood pressure; if you have or have had bronchial asthma; if you have had asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction to aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic; if it is for the treatment of pain before or after coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG); if you are 6 months or more pregnant; if you are breast-feeding; if you have inflammatory bowel disease such as Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis; or if you have had gastrointestinal bleeding or perforation during earlier treatment with a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have or have had a blood disorder; if you have a tendency to bleed; if you have or have had liver impairment or kidney impairment; if you have fluid retention or heart failure; if you have high blood pressure; if you have had hypersensitivity; if you have systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) or mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD); if you are an older person; if the user is a child aged 6 years or older; if you have stomach cancer or alcoholism; if you are in early or mid pregnancy or may be pregnant; if you have ischaemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease, cerebrovascular disease or risk factors for cardiovascular disease (for example high blood pressure, high blood lipids, diabetes, smoking); if you have hepatic porphyria; if you have had major surgery with blood loss; if you have a blood clotting disorder or are being given an anticoagulant; or if you have had hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to Yellow No. 5.

Considering the importance of the treatment, either stop breast-feeding or stop taking the medicine. Dizziness or fatigue may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery. When it is taken for a long period for an acute illness, as a rule this should be within 5 days.

Do not take it together with aspirin, another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic or high-dose methotrexate (15 mg a week or more) used as cancer treatment. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you take it together with a corticosteroid, alcohol, digoxin, phenytoin, probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, a sulfonylurea, an ACE inhibitor, an angiotensin II receptor antagonist, a diuretic, lithium, a coumarin anticoagulant (warfarin and the like), baclofen, an immunosuppressant (ciclosporin, tacrolimus, sirolimus), a thrombolytic, ticlopidine, an antithrombotic, a medicine that raises blood potassium (trimethoprim, heparin and the like), an inducer of CYP2C8 or CYP2C9 (for example rifampicin or phenobarbital), low-dose methotrexate (less than 15 mg a week), an antiplatelet medicine or a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor, or if you take low-dose aspirin to prevent myocardial infarction or stroke.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: rarely shock (chest discomfort, chills, difficulty breathing, a fall in blood pressure and the like); rarely blood disorders such as aplastic anaemia, haemolytic anaemia, granulocytopenia, leukopenia, agranulocytosis, pancytopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time) or eosinophilia; indigestion, abdominal distension, heartburn, upper abdominal pain, diarrhoea or constipation; occasionally loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain or stomach discomfort; rarely oesophagitis, oesophageal stricture, worsening of diverticula, non-specific haemorrhagic colitis, ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease, peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, bloody stools, gastritis or pancreatitis; very rarely thirst, stomatitis, erythema multiforme, systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) or hair loss; occasionally angioedema; rarely Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome); drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) of unknown frequency; occasionally rash, urticaria, itching or purpura; rarely triggering of an asthma attack, eczema, an anaphylactic reaction or a photosensitivity reaction; rarely jaundice, raised ALT, raised AST, raised ALP, abnormal liver function or hepatitis; occasionally rhinitis, bronchospasm or acute pneumonia; rarely visual disturbance such as scotoma or dark spots, hearing loss, tinnitus or taste disturbance; fatigue, drowsiness, headache or dizziness; occasionally anxiety, restlessness, confusion or depression; rarely aseptic meningitis, severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, a stiff neck, fever or disturbance of consciousness; rarely mental disturbance, agitation, excitement, disorientation or reversible toxic amblyopia; rarely a fall or rise in blood pressure, palpitations, reduced urine output, blood in the urine, protein in the urine, raised BUN or blood creatinine, high blood potassium, reduced urine volume, generalised oedema with breathlessness or lassitude; rarely renal papillary necrosis, nephrotic syndrome, interstitial nephritis, peripheral oedema, acute pulmonary oedema, fluid retention, high blood pressure, heart failure or reduced fertility in women; occasionally swelling around the eye sockets; very rarely malaise, fever, nosebleed or worsening of inflammation.
